ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the side length of the square $ABCD$ is $a$, and point $E$ is a moving point on side $AB$. Connect $ED$, and rotate $ED$ clockwise by $90^\circ$ around point $E$ to $EF$. Connect $DF$ and $CF$. Then, when the sum of $DF+CF$ takes the minimum value, what is the perimeter of $\triangle DCF$? (Express in an algebraic equation involving $a$)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw BF, and through F, draw FG $\perp$ to the extension of AB at point G, \\
since rotating ED clockwise by $90^\circ$ around point E gives EF, \\
therefore EF$\perp$DE, EF=DE, \\
therefore $\angle$DEA + $\angle$FEG = $\angle$DEA + $\angle$ADE = $90^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle$ADE = $\angle$FEG, \\
therefore $\triangle$AED $\cong$ $\triangle$GFE (AAS), \\
therefore FG=AE, AD=EG, \\
therefore AD=EG=AB, \\
therefore BG=AE=FG, \\
therefore $\angle$CBF=$\angle$GBF+$45^\circ$, i.e., point F moves along the angle bisector of $\angle$CBG. \\
Construct the symmetric point C$^{\prime }$ of C with respect to BF, then point C$^{\prime }$ lies on the extension of AB, hence when D, F, and C are collinear, DF+CF=DC is minimal. \\
since AD=a, AC$^{\prime }$=2a, \\
therefore DC$^{\prime }$= $\sqrt{5}$a, \\
therefore the minimum value of DF+CF is $\sqrt{5}$a, \\
therefore the perimeter of $\triangle$DCF is DF+CF+CD=$\sqrt{5}$a+a=($\sqrt{5}$+1)a. \\
Thus, the answer is: $\boxed{(\sqrt{5}+1)a}$.

ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the side length of the square $ABCD$ is $a$, and point $E$ is a moving point on side $AB$. Connect $ED$, and rotate $ED$ clockwise by $90^\circ$ around point $E$ to $EF$. Connect $DF$ and $CF$. Then, when the sum of $DF+CF$ takes the minimum value, what is the perimeter of $\triangle DCF$? (Express in an algebraic equation involving $a$)
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Draw $BF$, and through $F$, draw $FG \perp$ to the extension of $AB$ at point $G$. Since rotating $ED$ clockwise by $90^\circ$ around point $E$ gives $EF$, therefore $EF \perp DE$ and $EF=DE$. Therefore $\angle DEA + \angle FEG = \angle DEA + \angle ADE = 90^\circ$, so $\angle ADE = \angle FEG$. Therefore $\triangle AED \cong \triangle GFE$ (AAS), hence $FG=AE$ and $AD=EG$. Therefore $AD=EG=AB$, so $BG=AE=FG$. Therefore $\angle CBF=\angle GBF+45^\circ$, i.e., point $F$ moves along the angle bisector of $\angle CBG$. Construct the symmetric point $C'$ of $C$ with respect to $BF$; then point $C'$ lies on the extension of $AB$, hence when $D$, $F$, and $C$ are collinear, $DF+CF=DC'$ is minimal. Since $AD=a$ and $AC'=2a$, therefore $DC'=\sqrt{5}a$. Therefore the minimum value of $DF+CF$ is $\sqrt{5}a$, and the perimeter of $\triangle DCF$ is $DF+CF+CD=\sqrt{5}a+a=(\sqrt{5}+1)a$. Thus, the answer is $\boxed{(\sqrt{5}+1)a}$.

method.method_draft: Use a geometric locus and reflection route. From the image, read ABCD as a square with AB horizontal, AD vertical, E on AB, and EF perpendicular to ED after the rotation. Through F draw FG perpendicular to the extension of AB at G. From the text rotation, EF=ED and EF perpendicular to ED. Since AB=a, this gives BG=AE=FG, so F always lies on the fixed 45-degree ray from B, the angle bisector between the extension of AB and BC. Reflect C across this fixed ray BF to C'. Then FC=FC', and C' lies on the extension of AB beyond B; specifically BC=a reflects to BC'=a horizontally, so AC'=2a. raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, it is known that the side length of the square $ABCD$ is $a$, and point $E$ is a moving point on side $AB$. Connect $ED$, and rotate $ED$ clockwise by $90^\circ$ around point $E$ to $EF$. Connect $DF$ and $CF$. Then, when the sum of $DF+CF$ takes the minimum value, what is the perimeter of $\triangle DCF$? (Express in an algebraic equation involving $a$)
raw_record.answer: \textbf{Solution:} Draw $BF$, and through $F$, draw $FG \perp$ to the extension of $AB$ at point $G$. Since rotating $ED$ clockwise by $90^\circ$ around point $E$ gives $EF$, therefore $EF \perp DE$ and $EF=DE$. Therefore $\angle DEA + \angle FEG = \angle DEA + \angle ADE = 90^\circ$, so $\angle ADE = \angle FEG$. Therefore $\triangle AED \cong \triangle GFE$ (AAS), hence $FG=AE$ and $AD=EG$. Therefore $AD=EG=AB$, so $BG=AE=FG$. Therefore $\angle CBF=\angle GBF+45^\circ$, i.e., point $F$ moves along the angle bisector of $\angle CBG$. Construct the symmetric point $C'$ of $C$ with respect to $BF$; then point $C'$ lies on the extension of $AB$, hence when $D$, $F$, and $C$ are collinear, $DF+CF=DC'$ is minimal. Since $AD=a$ and $AC'=2a$, therefore $DC'=\sqrt{5}a$. Therefore the minimum value of $DF+CF$ is $\sqrt{5}a$, and the perimeter of $\triangle DCF$ is $DF+CF+CD=\sqrt{5}a+a=(\sqrt{5}+1)a$. Thus, the answer is $\boxed{(\sqrt{5}+1)a}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a square ABCD, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is at the upper right, D is at the upper left; E is located on the bottom side AB; connect from D to E, from E to F outside on the right side, and a right angle is marked at E, indicating that EF is perpendicular to ED; at the same time DF and CF are also connected in the figure, and F is located outside on the right side of the square. Reasoning: According to the coordinate method, set A=(0,0), B=(a,0), C=(a,a), D=(0,a), let E=(x,0), where 0≤x≤a. Vector ED=(-x,a). After rotating 90° clockwise, obtain EF=(a,x), so F=E+EF=(a+x,x). Thus DF=√((a+x)^2+(x-a)^2)=√(2a^2+2x^2), CF=√(x^2+(x-a)^2). Let u=x/a, then DF+CF=a[√(2(1+u^2))+√(2u^2-2u+1)]. Take the derivative with respect to u, obtaining S'(u)=√2·u/√(1+u^2)+(2u-1)/√(2u^2-2u+1). Set S'(u)=0, solving gives the valid interior point u=1/3. The values at endpoints u=0,1 are both larger, so the minimum value is attained at u=1/3. At this time DF=2√5a/3, CF=√5a/3, therefore DF+CF=√5a. Also CD=a, so the perimeter of triangle DCF is DF+CF+CD=√5a+a=(√5+1)a.
